description.narrative:
Insatsen innebär en andra fas i samarbetet mellan Sida och Sexual Violence Research Initiative (SVRI).
Stödet är på 32 MSEK för 4 år (2024­2027).
SVRI driver ett globalt nätverk för forskare, givare och andra aktörer som arbetar med mot könsrelaterat våld i låg­ och medelinkomstländer.
SVRI är en NGO med sekretariat i Sydafrika, global verksamhet och nästan 8000 medlemmar.
SVRI:s centrala verksamhet är att finansiera forskningsprojekt på nationell nivå och att underlätta lärande och nätverkande inom det tematiska området.
De fördelar 8­-10 forskningsanslag till forskare på landnivå i det globala syd årligen och de som beviljas finansiering erhåller också kapacitetsutvecklingsstöd.
SVRI arrangerar vartannat år en global konferens för att bygga och sprida kunskap runt effektiva sätt att förebygga våld.
The contribution is a second phase of cooperation with SVRI Violence Initiative. SVRI runs a global network of researchers in the area of prevention and elimination of gender based violence.

Vision:
SVRIs vision is a world free from violence against women (VAW), a world free from violence against children (VAC) and other forms of violence stemming from gender inequality.
Mission: To increase and strengthen action-oriented research and its uptake to improve and expand effective VAW and VAC prevention and response efforts globally.
Objectives: Building evidence for change, the SVRI: - Facilitates the co-creation of VAW and VAC research, practice and policy collaborations for evidence building through SVRI grant making. - Ensures research addresses research gaps identified by the field, for the field. - Tests new approaches for evidence building for impact at scale. - Contributes to systematic evidence building with a particular focus on ending child sexual violence in LMICs.
Empowering evidence builders through capacity strengthening, the SVRI: - Provides bespoke capacity strengthening and mentoring to SVRI Grantees. - Provides access to online courses, research methods and tools and datasets. - Models new approaches for capacity strengthening for research and impact at scale. - Grows the field for research through its SVRI Mentorship Programme.
Creating collective impact through global exchange and partnerships, the SVRI: - Hosts the bi-annual SVRI Forum: Connect | Learn | Share. - Hosts and builds the SVRI Knowledge Hub. - Is trauma informed and is an advocate for self and collective care. - Fosters SVRI membership.
Influencing and supporting structural change, the SVRI: - Engages donors and decision-makers on ethical resourcing and evidence-based decision making. - Promotes Feminist Funding via the SVRIs ethical funding for research in LMICs toolkit.
Aims (expected outcomes):
SVRI aim to: - Create a cooperative, nurturing field where information and knowledge are shared and individuals and organisations collaborate effectively with each other, including across fields and disciplines.
- Generate and mobilise more resources and ensure they are used effectively for research and evidence-based practice in LMICs.
- Grow rigorous research and innovations, tested by strong research designs for improved GBV response and prevention in LMICs that are replicated and taken to scale.
- Increase the number of LMIC researchers leading impactful and innovative research on VAW and VAC in LMICs.
- Increase the uptake of research findings among programme managers, funders, and policy makers for more impactful funding, policies, and programming in LMICs and beyond.

sector.narrative: Ending violence against women and girls

description.narrative:
In November 2024 the biannual SVRI Forum was conducted, this time in South Africa, with 1500 participants from 111 countries. 47 bursaries provided to for participants from LMIC. Sida was present at SVRI Forum and recognized it as key meeting place för learning and knowledge sharing about GBV.
SVRIs role as a global network with more than 12 000 members advancing knowledge and evidence on violence against women and children is showcased by the following activities in 2024: 6601 registrations to SVRIs online courses, 40 publications released and 27 webinars held, SVRI has 40 000 linked in followers.
Research Grants: 914 000 USD disbursed through 8 Research grants and additional 1 350 000 USD allocated to 10 new research grants. These grants will support research in Colombia, Malawi, Mauritius, Mongolia, South Africa, Sri Lanka, Tanzania, and Ukraine
In the report the feed back from a previous grantee is cited:
In the words of Shalini Joshi, Program Director at Meedan and a 2023 SVRI grant partner:
"The SVRI grant was more than just financial support. It was a partnership that respected our local knowledge and provided the mentorship we needed to navigate complex research challenges. This collaboration has been instrumental in amplifying our work on technology-facilitated gender-based violence."
SVRIs also reports on impact by showcasing how they together with grantees have translated research findings into lasting change. The examples range from trans inclusion in GBV work in Kazakhstan to GBV in higher education I Africa.
SVRIs work to ensure that the research they support is relevant is assessed to be comprehensive and relevant. SVRI is a key stakeholder on identifying and closing evidence gap. This is done both by leading work to settle broadly agreed research agendas and also by prioritizing underfinanced areas of research when selecting grantees. SVRI has in recent years expanded grants with focus on marginalised groups such as indigenous communities. LGBTI persons and displaced communities.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
